newsitem.title: JAPAN: SPEED SKATING-GAGNON STAKES CLAIM TO FOURTH WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-GAGNON STAKES CLAIM TO FOURTH WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Canada's Marc Gagnon began his quest for a fourth world overall title with a win in the men's 1,500 metres at the world short track speed skating championships on Friday.
Double Olympic gold medallist Chun Lee-Kyung of South Korea, who is attempting to win a third world crown, took the women's 1,500 metres.
Gagnon completed the course in two minutes, 21.322 seconds, ahead of Italians Orazio Fagone and Mirko Vuillermin. Fagone clocked 2:21.617 with Vuillermin another 0.446 seconds back.
"I felt strong at the end of the 1,500 today, so I feel I'm in good shape," said the 21-year-old from the northern Quebec town of Chicoutimi.
"I have confidence that I can win the world championships again, but there are a lot of good skaters here, so I'll have to work hard."
The women's 1,500 metres was an all-Asia affair with three South Koreans, two Chinese and a Japanese skater advancing to the semi-finals from a field of 29 competitors from 17 countries.
Chun, a 21-year-old university student who won overall titles last year and in 1994, battled with team mate Won Hye-Kyung for four laps before edging to the front on the final lap.
"I didn't expect her to go so fast," said Chun. "At first it was a bit stressful, but in the end it enabled me to win the race."
Chun, gold medallist in the 3,000 metres and relay events at the 1994 Olympics, finished in 2:29.426, edging Won by .128 seconds. Yang Yang of China was third.
